content: Individuals diagnosed with type 2 diabetes exhibit a heightened risk of sustaining fractures, particularly in the hip and other major bones, when compared to individuals without diabetes. Poor glycemic control, as indicated by an A1C level exceeding 9% over a two-year period, is strongly associated with an increased likelihood of fractures. Additionally, the use of certain glucose-lowering medications, such as thiazolidinediones, has been identified as a contributing factor to an elevated fracture risk.
